statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to the low band because December NQ futures have fully retraced their evening drift back to the settle, while Stress stays elevated on a 10-year Treasury yield that reached 5.227% late Thursday, its highest since 2007.
recommendation: December NQ futures print 30,767.00, +0.25 against the 30,766.75 settle, inside a 30,679.00-30,775.00 evening band on roughly 18.0k contracts. The gradual drift lower earlier in the session has been completely retraced, which is mean reversion working rather than failing, and it follows a cash session in which the Nasdaq-100 recovered a 0.87% decline in full to close at 30,478.86, up 0.03%. Two completed round trips in succession are the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures, so Tail eases to 17 in the low band. Stress is held at 56 because the macro backdrop deteriorated further overnight: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.227% late Thursday, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year touched 5.496%, both fresh 52-week highs, before easing to 5.193% and 5.476%. Against that, crude has extended its fade, with WTI near $93.27 and Brent near $105.63 after declines of 1.42% and 0.91%, as reporting continues on a phased US-Iran arrangement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz; that removes the amplifier that drove Thursday's yield surge. Volatility is contained with the VIX at 15.67 after fading from a 16.57 high, and latest-session index internals remain dispersed rather than aligned. Confidence is 87 on fresh verified futures, index, volatility, crude, yield, Asian-futures and calendar evidence; the shared Finviz context was about 116 minutes old and therefore stale under the provider contract, and it was also partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so all cross-asset confirmation came from independent primary sources.
headline: December NQ futures retrace the evening dip to 30,767.00, flat against settle; Tail eases to 17 as crude extends its fade
body: The Nasdaq-100 enters the Friday overnight session without the one-way structure that would change the Tail reading. Thursday's cash session traded down to 30,204.16, roughly 0.87% below the 30,470.29 previous close, then recovered the entire decline to a 30,529.35 high and settled at 30,478.86, up 8.56 points. Since the Globex reopen, December NQ futures first worked lower toward 30,679.00 and have now returned to 30,767.00 on roughly 18.0k contracts, leaving the contract flat against its 30,766.75 settle inside a band of about 96 points. The dominant background remains the global long-end bond rout, and it extended overnight: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.227% late Thursday, the highest since 2007, and the 30-year touched 5.496%, the highest since 2004, with both now marginally easier at 5.193% and 5.476%. The official H.15 release for 23 September put the 2-year at 4.85%, the 10-year at 5.11% and the 30-year at 5.40%, so the move has carried roughly a further eight to ten basis points since. Drivers cited for the selloff include rebounding oil, stronger-than-expected US PMI data and weak demand at a $70 billion five-year auction, and roughly 69% odds of a further rate increase by the end of October are discounted. Against that, crude has extended its fade: WTI trades near $93.27 and Brent near $105.63 after declines of 1.42% and 0.91%, as reports continue that US and Iranian negotiators are working toward a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Volatility remains contained, with the VIX at 15.67 after fading from a 16.57 session high. Asia is mixed, with Nikkei futures at 65,585 against a 65,513.99 close and Hang Seng futures at 24,627 against 24,761.13. Latest-session index internals stay dispersed, with Meta up 4.5% and Alphabet up 1.34% against Arm down 7.88% and Qualcomm down 1.51%, which undercuts the coordinated impulse a genuine Tail path usually requires. The named conditions that would change the Tail reading are a renewed crude leg back above Thursday's $94.61 settle, a disorderly extension of the long-end move during European hours, or observed shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after Friday's 13:30Z cash open.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the Claude Tail estimate ranged from 17 to 25 and spent most of the period in the watch band. The single orange print came at 09:00Z during the European morning, when a trend-down read pushed Tail to 25. From the US cash open onward the estimate drifted back down as the index recovered its intraday decline, and the window closed with six consecutive low-band readings of 19, 19, 19, 18, 18 and 18. Stress stayed elevated throughout, between 49 and 58, reflecting the continuing long-end yield rout rather than any observed breakdown in mean reversion.
outlookSummary: The overnight path runs through Asian and European hours with no scheduled US release until Friday's 12:30Z data block, so the conditional estimate stays in the low-to-watch band and rises mainly at liquidity transitions: the Tokyo close at 06:00Z and the European cash and bond open at 07:00Z, where a disorderly continuation of the long-end move is the most credible conditional route to persistent equity pressure. The concentrated window is 12:25Z to 14:15Z, covering August Durable Goods Orders at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open and final Michigan sentiment with its five-year inflation expectation at 14:00Z, which is the single most credible catalyst given a 10-year above 5%. Fed Williams speaks at 09:15Z as an earlier rate-path checkpoint. The published estimate steps down after the 20:00Z cash close and falls further from 21:00Z, when CME equity futures close for the week and no tradable price path remains; the residual weekend exposure is gap risk around the Strait of Hormuz talks and the Trump-Xi track rather than intraday Tail.
